column1:
- Positive drivers: “Job gains have been solid…unemployment rate has declined substantially,” and policy remains accommodative at a 0–0.25% funds rate with ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases. Narrative-based readings of FOMC communications (Romer and Romer) and the credit channel literature (Bernanke, Gertler, and Gilchrist) suggest such accommodation, especially via MBS, supports household credit and activity.
- Offsetting factors: Inflation “has exceeded 2 percent for some time,” and the Committee accelerates tapering. By the Taylor principle/Taylor rule tradition (Taylor; Clarida et al.), this foreshadows the need for policy rates to eventually rise more than one-for-one with inflation to anchor expectations, tempering the statement’s positivity.
- Market implication: As QE is tapered, the downward pressure on term premia eases; yield-curve research (Cochrane and Piazzesi) implies longer-dated yields could firm, making overall financial conditions marginally less supportive than before.

Overall, the communication is mildly positive on growth and employment but moderated by inflation risks and the beginning of policy normalization.
